• Engineer automated model validation, regression testing, QA frameworks, drift detection, and production reliability mechanisms.
• Enable cloud-ready training pipelines and hybrid-cloud execution with performance, scalability, and cost efficiency in mind.
• Advance observability and intelligent automation, including automated RCA, knowledge graphs, and AI-assisted operational workflows.

• 8+ years of software engineering experience with a strong track record as a senior individual contributor delivering complex platforms or distributed systems.
• Advanced Python skills and strong software design, debugging, and performance-engineering fundamentals.
• Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Docker, Linux, infrastructure automation, and production operations.
• Experience designing large-scale distributed systems, data-processing platforms, or ML training infrastructure.
• Strong understanding of MLOps, ML training pipelines, model deployment, lifecycle automation, and CI/CD.
• Experience with Apache Spark, Hadoop, or comparable distributed data-processing technologies.
• Ability to make architecture trade-offs, independently lead complex technical initiatives, and influence teams without direct authority.

Good to Have:
• Experience building internal ML platforms used by multiple engineering or data science teams.
• Familiarity with LightGBM, XGBoost, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Weights & Biases, or MLflow.
• Experience with GPU computing, CUDA, NVIDIA Triton, or optimized model-serving systems.
• Experience with AWS, hybrid-cloud infrastructure, feature stores, model registries, and automated retraining.
• Exposure to Generative AI, LLMs, RAG, AI agents, and knowledge graphs.
• Experience in AdTech, real-time bidding, or other high-throughput, latency-sensitive environments.

AI-Enabled Engineering Mindset:

We value engineers who actively leverage Generative AI tools and IDEs (e.g. GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Windsurf etc.) to accelerate development, improve code quality, automate repetitive tasks, and enhance documentation and debugging workflows. Engineers who demonstrate AI-first thinking using these tools to drive faster experimentation, ideation, and technical execution will thrive in our high-scale, performance-critical environment.

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering (CS/IT) or an equivalent degree from a well-known institute or university; advanced degree is a plus but not required given depth of experience.

Job Summary
The Staff Engineer is the senior individual contributor at Mindtickle. The role is defined by scope, not tenure or technology.

Staff Engineers shape technical direction across teams. They take on problems that cross system boundaries, i.e., foundational platform decisions, architectural work that spans multiple services, performance and reliability challenges that no single team owns, and AI capabilities that need to be woven into the product rather than bolted on.

This is not a senior engineer with a different title. The role exists for a different category of problem.

Key Responsibility
Solve Organization wide problems - crisply define the problem, propose the solution, implement it and get it adopted. One of the finest examples of this is the data platform at Mindtickle.

Take on problems that span teams — performance regressions across services, integration patterns that cut across domains, AI capabilities that have to hold up across varied customer configurations.

Review designs from other teams. Identify architectural risks before they become incidents. Propose and drive migrations, deprecations, and platform investments.

Set the technical standard through your work — the code you write, the design documents you publish, the reviews you give. Influence through clarity, not authority.

Be the champion of AI transformation at Mindtickle. Evaluate where AI-native approaches should replace or augment traditional systems. Reasons about cost, latency, reliability, explainability, and maintenance burden. Help shape how the engineering organization itself uses AI tooling.

Own the operational health of the systems you influence. Drive reliability, observability, and performance work proactively, with data and clear proposals.

Make other engineers better — through design reviews, technical mentorship, and creating clarity in areas where others are stuck. Distribute knowledge rather than concentrate it.

Required Qualification
Clear evidence of significant industry experience as an individual contributor in software engineering, with the most recent years operating at Staff scope or equivalent. Scope is defined by the kind of problem owned, not the title held.

Demonstrated architectural ownership. Evidence that you have defined or significantly shaped system architecture in production that has stood the test of time — structural decisions you made, not designs you implemented.

Cross-team technical influence. Concrete examples where your work has shaped systems beyond your immediate team and thrived — patterns adopted by others, disagreements resolved across boundaries, design proposals taken up by other teams.

Production discipline. Direct ownership of systems running in production, with demonstrated work on reliability, observability, or operational improvement that survived contact with real customers.

Incident management. Track record of leading the response to production incidents — driving diagnosis under pressure, owning the post-incident review, and translating findings into structural improvements that prevent recurrence.

Strong written technical communication. Design documents, RFCs, or technical proposals that articulate complex trade-offs in writing.

Depth in at least one domain: multi-tenant SaaS systems, integration-heavy platforms, workflow or rules engines, configuration-driven architectures, real-time analytics, data pipelines, or platform infrastructure serving multiple internal teams.

Judgment on complexity. A record of making systems simpler — deprecations led, abstractions removed, boring technology chosen where it sufficed.

Preferred Qualification
9+ years of industry experience in software engineering, with multiple years operating at Staff scope or equivalent.

Experience leading large-scale migrations or platform transitions that affected multiple teams.

Familiarity with AWS and the architectural patterns relevant at scale — multi-region or multi-AZ design, managed data services, identity and security boundaries, cost-aware infrastructure choices.

Understanding of product metrics and product analytics — how systems are instrumented to support product decisions, how telemetry shapes prioritization, and how engineering choices surface in business outcomes.

Open-source contributions to systems-level projects — databases, infrastructure, runtime, build, observability — rather than feature contributions to consumer products.

Published technical writing — engineering blog posts, conference talks with substantive material, RFCs, design documents, and / or conference papers.

Experience in environments where customer variation is a first-class constraint — meaningfully different customer configurations, integrations, or data shapes within a single product line.

The Impact of a Sr Security Engineer at Coupa:

Coupa's Security Engineers keep our enterprise, product, platform, and customer data safe. As a Senior Security Engineer, you'll take ownership of complex, ambiguous security problems end to end — building cloud security controls, setting engineering standards, and partnering closely with Engineering, IT, and Compliance to ship durable, automated security tooling rather than one-off fixes. You'll set the technical standard for how the team remediates and automates, and you'll be a go-to resource other engineers turn to when a finding needs real root-cause analysis instead of a quick workaround.

What You'll Do:
• Design and implement multi-cloud security controls across Coupa's cloud environment, including VPC segmentation, security groups/NACLs, IAM policy design using least-privilege and permission boundaries, and Organizations/SCPs for guardrails at scale.
• Build policy as code and IaC security guardrails and wire them into CI/CD as pre-merge and pre-deploy gates rather than after-the-fact reviews.
• Harden containerized workloads and Kubernetes clusters — image scanning, admission control, pod security standards, network policies, and container/workload runtime detection.
• Own vulnerability analysis of application packages, container images, and third-party dependencies; triage findings by exploitability and business impact rather than CVSS score alone.
• Design and implement remediations (not just report findings) including secure code fixes, cloud configuration changes, and IAM policy adjustments using least-privilege principles.
• Support incident response and forensics as a technical contributor — log analysis, root-cause investigation, and remediation validation using cloud-native and EDR tooling.
• Partner with the Risk & Compliance team to provide technical evidence and control validation for audit frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP).
• Support and mentor other security engineers — reviewing designs and remediation plans, sharing root-cause analysis techniques, and helping less experienced teammates work through complex or ambiguous findings.
• Participate in the on-call/incident rotation and help continuously improve remediation and response runbooks.

What You Will Bring to Coupa:
• 5+ years of experience in security engineering or cloud operations, with a track record of independently owning complex assessments from scoping through remediation.
• Practical experience with cloud security fundamentals (AWS, GCP, or Azure) — IAM, networking, and common misconfiguration classes — sufficient to both find and fix cloud findings.
• Strong scripting/automation skills in Python, Bash, or JavaScript, with experience building or extending internal security tooling.
• Experience with dependency/container vulnerability scanning tools and integrating them into CI/CD pipelines.
• Working knowledge of common compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP) and what auditable evidence looks like.
• Critical thinking and root-cause analysis skills — comfortable digging past a scanner's output to understand and explain why a vulnerability exists.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills for translating technical findings into remediation guidance for engineers and risk context for stakeholders.
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
• Relevant certifications a plus: CISSP, CCSP, CISA, or AWS/GCP security certifications.
